title: Find a method by its exact signature

blocks.text: `getDeclaredMethod(name, types...)` wants the **exact** parameter types. Autoboxing does not apply to lookup: a method `add(int, int)` is not found with `Integer.class, Integer.class`. With overloads the types pick the method. `getDeclaredMethod` searches only the class itself, and `getMethod` finds public methods only.

items: `find(type, name, params...)`: the method with exactly these parameter types, declared on `type` or **any superclass** at **any access level**, or `Optional.empty()`.
`overloads(type, name)`: `"name(Type,Type)"` (simple type names, no spaces) for every method `type` itself declares with that name, **private ones too**, sorted.

blocks.text: With `Base { private String secret(); }` and `MathOps extends Base { public int add(int,int); public double add(double,double); private long add(long,long); ... }`:

cases.says: find(MathOps, "add", int, int) is the int version, a missing name is empty, and overloads(MathOps, "scale") lists both public overloads.
find(MathOps, "add", Integer, Integer) is empty: add takes int, and lookup does not box.
find(MathOps, "secret") finds the private method MathOps inherits from Base.
overloads(MathOps, "add") holds the private add(long,long) as well as the two public ones.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Method and constructor lookup needs the exact parameter types, so Integer.class does not find an int parameter, and overloads are told apart by their types.
getMethods() and getConstructors() return public members only, while the getDeclared...() family returns the class's own members at every access level.
